This is an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act read with Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking condonation of delay of 1292 days in filing the present appeal.
For the reasons mentioned in the application, same is allowed.
The delay of 1292 days in filing the present appeal is condoned.

The present revision petition has been filed against the judgment dated 14.07.2014 passed by the Sessions Judge, Jind vide which the appeal preferred by the accused-petitioner against the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 22.11.2011 passed by the Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Safidon has been dismissed.

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case are that the accused-petitioner had borrowed a sum of Rs.6,30,000/-
orally from the complainant- respondent No.2 with an assurance to return the same in near future.

In order to discharge his liability, the accused-petitioner issued a cheque bearing No.486724 dated 30.10.2009 for a sum of Rs.6,30,000/- drawn at Punjab National Bank, Ratgal, Kurukshetra in favour of the complainant-respondent No.2.

On presentation of the aforesaid cheque by the complainant with his banker, namely, Punjab National Bank, Safidon, the same was not encashed and was dishonoured with the remarks 'funds insufficient' vide a return memo dated 30.10.2009.

On the request of the accused-petitioner, the complainant-respondent presented the aforesaid cheque once again with his bank but the same was again dishonoured with the remarks 'funds insufficient' vide a memo dated 30.11.2009.
The accused-petitioner was served with a legal notice dated 03.12.2009 for making the payment within 15 days of receipt of the said notice but the accused-petitioner failed to do so.

Thus, he cheated the complainant-respondent No.2 which led to initiation of proceedings under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 read with Section 420 IPC.
3.

In the complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 filed by the complainant/respondent No.2, the accused/petitioner was summoned to face trial under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.
The evidence was led and ultimately, the accused/petitioner was held guilty and accordingly, convicted for the offence punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.

The accused-petitioner was directed to make the payment of the entire cheque 2 of 5 CRR-1564-2018 (O & M) ::3::
amount of Rs.6,30,000/- to the complainant-respondent No.2 till 31.03.2012 failing which he was to undergo imprisonment for one year.

4. Aggrieved against the said judgment of conviction and order of sentence, the accused/petitioner preferred an appeal before the Sessions Judge, Jind which came to be dismissed vide a judgment dated 14.07.2014.
5. Still aggrieved, the present revision petition has been preferred by the accused-petitioner.

6. The learned counsel for the petitioner contends that during the pendency of the present petition, a compromise has been effected between the parties, pursuant to which both the parties were directed to appear before the Chief Judicial Magistrate concerned on 07.08.2025 vide order dated 07.07.2025 passed by this Court for recording their statements as per certain parameters mentioned in the said order.
He also contends that in pursuance to the order dated 07.07.2025, a report of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jind, dated 27.08.2025 has been received.
As per the said report, both the parties have appeared before the concerned Court on 25.08.2025 and got recorded their respective statements.
A perusal of the aforesaid report would show that the parties have effected a genuine compromise without there being any pressure, coercion or undue influence.

As per Para 01 of the compromise/affidavit dated 12.05.2023, the complainant-respondent No.2 has received an amount Surender Singh Rana vs State Of Haryana And Ors on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5264207/
2 of Rs.6,30,000/- as full and final payment.

sentences.text: Thus, nothing remains due towards the complainant-respondent No.2.

He further contends that in view of Section 147 of the Negotiable Instruments Act read with Section 320 Cr.P.C. where a settlement has been effected, the offence under Section 138 3 of 5 CRR-1564-2018 (O & M) ::4::
of the Negotiable Instruments Act can be compounded on account of the fact that a mutual compromise has been effected between the parties.

7. The learned counsel for the State-respondent No.1 and the counsel for the complainant-respondent No.2 contend that as the matter has been settled between the parties, they have no objection if the prayer of the learned counsel for accused-petitioner for compounding the offence under Section 138 N.I. Act is allowed and the petitioner is acquitted of the charges framed against him.
8. I have heard the learned counsel for both the parties.

9. This Hon'ble Court in 'Ramesh Chander Vs. State of Haryana and another, 2007(1)
RCR (Criminal) 245' held as under:-
"4.

entities.text:
Ramesh Chander Vs. State of Haryana and another, 2007(1)
RCR (Criminal) 245
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the provisions of Section 147 of the Act, the offence under Section 138 is compoundable.

Section 147 reads as under:
"Offence to be compoundable- Notwithstanding anything contained in the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973(2 of 1974), every offence punishable under this Act shall be compoundable".
5.

The compounding of the offence under Section 138 can be done during the trial of the case as well as by the High Court or Court of Session while acting in the exercise of its power of revision under Section 401 Criminal Procedure Code Reference may be made to Section 320(6) Criminal Procedure Code in this regard.
6. Further, under Section 320(8) Criminal Procedure Code the composition of an offence shall have the effect of acquittal of the accused with whom the offence has been compounded."

This Court in 'Vatsa Electronics Vs. Pala Ram & Anr. decided on 09.03.2022 in CRR-1585-2019' has also held that once a settlement is being effected, then in terms of Section 147 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and Section 320 Cr.P.C., the accused ought to be acquitted as the offence stands compounded.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. In view of the above, since, the parties have voluntarily settled the disputes between themselves, it is a fit case for allowing them to compound the offence.
